note: What an operator part way through typing an address could have meant, and the runs of a formula that read like one. Completion runs against the schema rather than against the slots an object carries, so the case whose object is missing a slot the schema declares still offers it, and a refusal later names a real problem rather than the completion hiding it. The candidates are a list, so their order is compared: a document variable is offered ahead of an object name, and the cells of a table come back in the order the schema enumerates them rather than sorted. The fill is the run every candidate starts with, measured in the units a JavaScript string counts. So is every offset a run of a formula reports, which is what a host highlights by. The case whose source opens with a character outside the basic plane puts the run that follows at offset 7 rather than at 6, and a byte offset or a character offset would put it somewhere else again. Matching ignores case by cutting the value to the length of what was typed and folding that, rather than folding first. The two part where a character folds to a different number of units. The whole of the folding the two engines do agrees: every character of the basic plane and of the two planes above it folds alike in both, measured over 1488 mappings, and the case that completes against a name spelled in capitals rests on that.
